subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What identity and compatibility contract should OpenClaw use for inbound media isolation across agents and channels?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the durable security boundary affects existing media refs, storage layout, sandbox staging, plugin/channel callers, and possibly provenance metadata.

options.title: Managed scoped media contract
options.body: Define a core-owned scoped/provenanced inbound-media contract and migrate channel callers, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests around that single contract.

options.title: Narrow account subdirectories
options.body: Scope writes by channel account ID first, accepting that resolver, staging, and compatibility follow-up must be carefully completed to avoid partial isolation.

options.title: Persist provenance index
options.body: Keep flat files but add a durable media provenance/index layer with explicit privacy, retention, and resolver semantics.

recommendation.title: Managed scoped media contract
recommendation.body: Define a core-owned scoped/provenanced inbound-media contract and migrate channel callers, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests around that single contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history on the core media store, media-reference, and sandbox-staging boundary that the decision must cover.
